_meta.description: Verified general legal information for students in Germany, used by Student Rights Check. Every statement the tool makes must come from this file. Nothing here is advice for an individual case.
_meta.verified_by: Manual check against law texts and official/authoritative sources listed in each entry
_meta.region_note: Federal law applies everywhere. University (exam) rules are verified for Bavaria (RaPO / BayHIG / AGVwGO); housing values marked 'München' are Munich-specific.

exam_sick_withdrawal.title: Sick on exam day: withdraw immediately with a doctor's certificate
exam_sick_withdrawal.summary: At Bavarian universities of applied sciences, the reasons for withdrawing from or missing an exam must be reported to the university immediately (unverzüglich) in writing and made credible. For illness you need a medical certificate based on an examination that, as a rule, took place on the exam day itself. Courts apply a strict standard: reporting weeks later is too late. Many universities accept the certificate up to the third day after the exam, but check your own APO.

exam_appeal.title: Disagree with an exam decision: objection or lawsuit, your choice
exam_appeal.summary: In Bavaria, against a personal exam decision (e.g. a failed exam) you may choose to either file an objection (Widerspruch) with the university or go directly to the administrative court. The deadline is normally one month and is stated in the legal remedy notice (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung) of the decision. Against an exmatriculation after finally failing, only a lawsuit is possible (Art. 12 Abs. 2 AGVwGO).

exam_inspection.title: You can usually see your marked exam
exam_inspection.summary: An exam is an administrative procedure. Exam regulations normally give students the right to inspect their marked exam, the examiner's comments and oral exam protocols after the result is published. Where and how long you can do this is set in your university's exam regulations, so check your APO/SPO and ask the exam office. Inspecting your exam is usually the first step before an objection.

exam_disadvantage_comp.title: Chronic illness or disability: you can apply for Nachteilsausgleich
exam_disadvantage_comp.summary: Students with a disability or chronic (also psychological) illness can apply for adjustments in exams (Nachteilsausgleich), e.g. more time or a separate room. In Bavaria this follows from the Bavarian Higher Education Innovation Act (BayHIG) and the exam regulations. You apply in advance with a medical certificate. A short-term illness is not a reason for Nachteilsausgleich; then withdrawing from the exam is the right path.

exam_maternity.title: Pregnant students are protected by the Maternity Protection Act
exam_maternity.summary: Since 2018 the Maternity Protection Act also applies to students. During the protection period (normally 6 weeks before and 8 weeks after birth) you have the right not to take exams and are exempt from compulsory courses, excursions and lab work. You can choose to take part anyway with a written declaration, which you can withdraw at any time.

minimum_wage.title: Minimum wage applies to Werkstudenten and Minijobs too
minimum_wage.summary: The statutory minimum wage is 13.90 EUR gross per hour from 1 January 2026 and 14.60 EUR from 1 January 2027. It applies to working students and mini-jobbers as well.

internship_wage.title: Internships: when you must get minimum wage
internship_wage.summary: Interns are generally entitled to minimum wage. Exceptions: a compulsory internship required by your study regulations, an orientation internship of up to 3 months before studies, and a first voluntary internship of up to 3 months alongside your studies with the same company. A voluntary internship longer than 3 months must be paid minimum wage from day one.

werkstudent_20h.law: Werkstudentenprivileg (§ 6 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 SGB V, § 27 Abs. 4 SGB III)
werkstudent_20h.title: Werkstudent: max. 20 hours a week during the semester
werkstudent_20h.summary: As a Werkstudent you pay no health, care or unemployment insurance contributions from your job (only pension insurance) as long as you work no more than 20 hours a week during the lecture period. More hours are fine in the semester break, at evenings, nights or weekends, but in total not more than 26 weeks a year above 20 hours. The amount you earn does not matter.

minijob_limit.title: Minijob earnings limit: 603 EUR a month in 2026
minijob_limit.summary: A Minijob may pay on average at most 603 EUR a month in 2026 (7,236 EUR a year) and 633 EUR from 2027. The limit is linked to the minimum wage. Minijobbers have the same rights as other employees: paid holiday, sick pay, minimum wage.

sick_pay.title: Sick pay: up to 6 weeks, also for Werkstudenten and Minijobs
sick_pay.summary: If you cannot work because of illness, your employer must keep paying your wage for up to six weeks per illness. The right starts after the job has lasted four weeks without interruption. It applies to part-time, Werkstudent and Minijob employees just like full-time staff.

minimum_vacation.title: Minimum paid holiday: 4 weeks per year, also part-time
minimum_vacation.summary: Every employee, including Werkstudenten and Minijobbers, has at least 24 working days of paid holiday per year based on a 6-day week. For fewer working days it is calculated pro rata: days per week x 24 / 6 (e.g. 2 days a week = 8 days, 3 days = 12 days, 5 days = 20 days).

probation_max.title: Notice periods: 2 weeks in probation (max. 6 months), then 4 weeks
probation_max.summary: During an agreed probation period, the job can be ended with two weeks' notice, but for at most six months. After that the normal notice period applies: four weeks to the 15th or the end of a month.

written_termination.title: Termination of a job must be on paper and signed
written_termination.summary: Ending an employment relationship by notice or termination agreement requires written form (signed paper). Electronic form is excluded, so a termination by e-mail or WhatsApp is not valid.

payslip_reference.title: You have a right to a payslip and a job reference
payslip_reference.summary: With every wage payment you are entitled to a payslip in text form showing the period and how your pay is made up. When the job ends, you are entitled to a reference (Arbeitszeugnis); on request a qualified one that also rates your performance and conduct. This also applies to student jobs.

working_hours.title: Working time: max. 8 (10) hours a day, breaks, 11 hours rest
working_hours.summary: Working time may normally not exceed 8 hours per working day; up to 10 hours are allowed if the average over 6 months stays at 8. If you work more than 6 hours you need at least 30 minutes break (45 minutes above 9 hours); you may not work more than 6 hours in a row without a break. Breaks can be split into blocks of at least 15 minutes. Between two shifts you need at least 11 hours of rest.

short_term_job.title: Holiday job: up to 3 months or 70 working days without social contributions
short_term_job.summary: A short-term job (kurzfristige Beschäftigung), e.g. a semester-break job, is free of social insurance contributions if it is limited in advance to at most 3 months or 70 working days in a calendar year, regardless of pay. All short-term jobs in the year are added up. It is still taxable, but you can usually get the tax back with a tax return.

equal_pay_parttime.title: Same job, same hourly pay: Minijobbers can't be paid less
equal_pay_parttime.summary: Part-time employees, including Minijobbers and working students, may not be treated worse than comparable full-time staff without an objective reason. The Federal Labour Court decided in January 2023 that a Minijobber with the same qualification and the same tasks must get the same hourly wage as full-time colleagues.

interview_questions.title: Job interview: forbidden questions and the 'right to lie'
interview_questions.summary: Employers may only ask questions related to the job. Questions about pregnancy or family planning, religion, sexual orientation, party or union membership are generally not allowed. If you are asked such a question, you may refuse or even answer untruthfully (the courts' 'right to lie') without the employer being able to cancel your contract later for that reason. Questions about qualifications, languages or work permit are allowed and must be answered truthfully.

intl_work_days.title: Non-EU students: 140 full or 280 half working days per year
intl_work_days.summary: With a student residence permit (§ 16b AufenthG) you may work up to 140 full days or 280 half days per calendar year without approval of the employment agency. A half day is up to 4 hours. Student assistant jobs at the university (studentische Nebentätigkeit) are not counted. Voluntary internships count, compulsory internships do not. Working more than allowed can put your permit at risk, so ask the Ausländerbehörde or the international office if unsure.

deposit_max.title: Deposit is capped at 3 months' cold rent
deposit_max.summary: For a flat or WG room, the deposit (Kaution) may be at most three times the monthly rent without operating costs (Nettokaltmiete). An agreement that is worse for the tenant is invalid, and you can claim back the part above the limit.

deposit_installments.title: You may pay the deposit in 3 monthly parts
deposit_installments.summary: If the deposit is a sum of money, the tenant is entitled to pay it in three equal monthly instalments. The first is due when the tenancy starts, the others together with the next rent payments. The landlord must keep the deposit separate from his own money in a bank account. A clause demanding the full amount up front cannot take this right away.

deposit_return.title: Getting your deposit back after moving out
deposit_return.summary: There is no fixed legal deadline for returning the deposit. The landlord gets a reasonable time to check his claims, usually about 3 to 6 months, sometimes longer if a utility bill (Nebenkostenabrechnung) is still due, for which he may keep a reasonable part. His claims for damage to the flat expire six months after he gets the flat back (§ 548 BGB). After that time, ask in writing for a deposit statement and payment with a deadline. Your own claim expires after three years.

tenant_notice.title: Tenant notice period is 3 months
tenant_notice.summary: A tenant can give notice by the third working day of a month, effective at the end of the month after next (about 3 months). A longer notice period to the tenant's disadvantage is invalid. Exceptions exist, e.g. for furnished rooms inside the landlord's own flat (§ 549 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 BGB) and for agreed waivers of notice, so this one is worth getting checked.

rent_brake.title: Mietpreisbremse: new rent max. 10% above local comparative rent
rent_brake.summary: In areas with a tight housing market, the rent at the start of a new tenancy may be at most 10% above the local comparative rent (in Munich: the Mietspiegel). In Bavaria this applies in 285 cities and municipalities including Munich and is extended until 31 December 2029. Exceptions exist (new buildings first rented after 1 Oct 2014, comprehensive modernisation, higher previous rent), and the landlord must tell you about them before signing.

rent_increase_cap.title: Rent increase cap: max. 15% in 3 years in Munich
rent_increase_cap.summary: In an ongoing tenancy the landlord can ask you to agree to an increase up to the local comparative rent, but in Munich (and other listed Bavarian municipalities) the rent may not rise by more than 15% within three years (instead of 20% elsewhere). Increases due to modernisation follow other rules.

rent_reduction.title: Defects (mould, pests, no heating): the rent is reduced by law
rent_reduction.summary: If the flat has a defect that reduces its use, e.g. mould, a pest infestation (cockroaches, mice, bedbugs) or no heating, the rent is reduced by law for as long as the defect exists. You must report the defect to the landlord immediately; if you do not, you can lose the right to reduce. In residential leases this right cannot be excluded by contract (§ 536 Abs. 4 BGB). How much you may reduce depends on the case, and paying too little can risk a termination, so get advice before cutting the rent.

landlord_entry.title: Your landlord may not enter your room without your consent
landlord_entry.summary: Once you rent a flat or room, you hold the right to decide who enters. The landlord needs a concrete reason (e.g. repairs, meter reading, viewing for a sale), must announce the visit in advance (often at least 24 hours, for viewings longer) and needs your consent. Only in a real emergency (burst pipe, gas leak, fire) may he enter without asking. Contract clauses allowing entry at any time without notice are invalid.

sublet.title: Subletting part of your flat: you can ask for permission
sublet.summary: If after signing the lease you get a legitimate interest (e.g. saving money, a semester abroad), you can demand the landlord's permission to sublet part of your flat. You always need the permission first. Since a BGH ruling of January 2026, subletting to make a profit is not a legitimate interest. A clause that excludes this right is invalid (§ 553 Abs. 3 BGB).

registration.title: Register your address within 2 weeks; the landlord must confirm
registration.summary: When you move into a flat, you must register at the registration office (Bürgerbüro / KVR in Munich) within two weeks. The landlord or main tenant must give you a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung within two weeks; a rental contract does not replace it. Missing these duties can be fined up to 1,000 EUR, on both sides.

cosmetic_repairs.law: § 307, § 535 BGB; BGH VIII ZR 185/14, VIII ZR 361/03
cosmetic_repairs.title: Moved into an unrenovated flat: you usually don't have to paint when you leave
cosmetic_repairs.summary: If you got the flat or room unrenovated and without fair compensation, a standard clause making you do the cosmetic repairs (painting, wallpapering) is invalid (BGH, 18 March 2015). Clauses with rigid schedules (e.g. 'kitchen every 3 years') are also invalid, as are clauses making you pay a share of future repairs when you move out early. Then the landlord can only demand the flat back in the state you received it. You must be able to prove that it was unrenovated, so take photos at move-in.

utility_bill.title: Utility bill (Nebenkostenabrechnung): 12-month deadlines for both sides
utility_bill.summary: The landlord must send the utility bill at the latest 12 months after the end of the billing period. If it arrives later, he can usually no longer demand extra payments (unless he is not responsible for the delay). You in turn have 12 months after receiving the bill to raise objections; after that you generally cannot. You may ask to see the receipts before you pay.

fixed_term_lease.title: Fixed-term lease only with a written reason, otherwise it is open-ended
fixed_term_lease.summary: A residential lease can only be limited in time if the landlord tells you a legal reason in writing when signing (e.g. he wants to live there himself or will renovate/demolish). Without such a reason the lease counts as open-ended, and you can give the normal 3-month notice. Furnished rooms in the landlord's own flat and short-term rentals follow different rules.

landlord_termination.title: The landlord needs a legal reason to give you notice
landlord_termination.summary: In a normal (open-ended) lease the landlord can only give ordinary notice if he has a legitimate interest, e.g. personal need (Eigenbedarf) or serious breaches by the tenant. Notice to raise the rent is not allowed. His notice period is at least 3 months and grows to 6 months after 5 years and 9 months after 8 years. Exceptions apply to furnished rooms in the landlord's own flat.

tenant_selfdisclosure.title: Flat applications: some questions a landlord may not ask
tenant_selfdisclosure.summary: In a tenant self-disclosure (Mieterselbstauskunft) landlords may ask about income, profession, household size and pets. Questions about religion, ethnic origin or political views are not allowed. You also have the right to know which of your data the landlord stores, why and for how long.

bafoeg.title: BAföG: up to 992 EUR a month in 2026
bafoeg.summary: The maximum BAföG for students not living with their parents is 992 EUR a month (475 EUR basic need + 380 EUR housing + health/care insurance supplement). Half is a grant, half an interest-free loan. BAföG is not paid retroactively before the month you apply, so apply early. A reform with higher rates is planned; according to the government draft of August 2026 the first increase comes on 1 April 2027 (not yet law).

kindergeld.title: Kindergeld continues during studies until age 25
kindergeld.summary: Parents receive Kindergeld of 259 EUR a month (2026) for a child in education or university studies up to the 25th birthday. During a first degree, side jobs do not affect it. Kindergeld is only paid retroactively for 6 months from the application.

broadcast_fee.title: Rundfunkbeitrag: exemption with BAföG (not living with parents)
broadcast_fee.summary: The broadcasting fee (18.36 EUR a month per flat) applies to every household. Students who receive BAföG and do not live with their parents can apply to be exempt. Without BAföG, a hardship application (Härtefall) is possible if your income is very low. In a WG the fee is paid once per flat, so share it.

tax_refund.title: Student job: you can often get your wage tax back
tax_refund.summary: Up to 12,348 EUR taxable income in 2026 no income tax is due for a single person. If wage tax was deducted from your student job, you can usually get it back by filing a tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung) for that year, e.g. via ELSTER. You can file voluntarily for the past four years.

wohngeld.title: Wohngeld: only if you are not eligible for BAföG in principle
wohngeld.summary: Students who are eligible for BAföG in principle get no housing benefit (Wohngeld), even if they receive no BAföG because their parents earn too much. Wohngeld is possible if BAföG is excluded in principle (e.g. age limit exceeded, maximum funding period over, late change of subject) or if BAföG is paid only as a full loan. You first need a BAföG rejection 'dem Grunde nach' from the BAföG office.

basic_account.title: Every person living legally in the EU has a right to a basic bank account
basic_account.summary: Banks offering accounts to consumers must open a basic account (Basiskonto) for anyone legally resident in the EU, including people without a fixed address and asylum seekers. It works on a credit basis (no overdraft) and offers deposits, withdrawals, transfers, direct debits and a debit card. Useful for international students whose application was rejected.

health_insurance.title: Health insurance: family insurance until 25, student rate until 30
health_insurance.summary: Health insurance is compulsory to enrol. Until your 25th birthday you can be insured free of charge through your parents' public insurance, if you earn at most 565 EUR a month (603 EUR in a Minijob) in 2026. After that, the student health insurance (KVdS) at a reduced rate applies, at most until the end of the semester in which you turn 30. After that you continue as a voluntary member at higher rates.

withdrawal_online.title: Bought online or by phone: 14 days to withdraw
withdrawal_online.summary: For contracts made online, by phone or at your door you can withdraw within 14 days without giving reasons. For goods the period starts when you receive them. If the seller did not inform you properly about this right, it lasts up to 12 months and 14 days. Declare the withdrawal clearly, e.g. by e-mail; just sending the item back is not always enough.

auto_renewal.title: Contracts may not silently renew for another fixed term
auto_renewal.summary: For consumer contracts concluded since 1 March 2022 (gym, phone, streaming, magazines...), a standard clause that automatically renews the contract for another fixed period is invalid. Automatic renewal is only allowed for an indefinite period, and the customer must then be able to cancel at any time with max. one month's notice.

consumer_notice.title: Notice before the end of the minimum term: max. 1 month
consumer_notice.summary: For consumer contracts concluded since 1 March 2022, a standard clause requiring notice of more than one month before the end of the initial term is invalid.

phone_contract.title: Phone and internet contracts: max. 24 months, then cancel monthly
phone_contract.summary: The initial term of a mobile or internet contract may not exceed 24 months, and the provider must also offer a contract of max. 12 months. After the initial term, a contract that renews silently can be cancelled at any time with one month's notice, at no cost. Early 'extensions' may not push the total binding term beyond 24 months.

cancel_button.title: Online subscriptions: a 'cancel contract' button is mandatory
cancel_button.summary: Companies that let consumers sign up for ongoing contracts on a website must also offer an easy online cancellation button ('Verträge hier kündigen' → 'jetzt kündigen'). If they don't, you can cancel at any time without notice. When ordering online, the final button must clearly say that you pay ('zahlungspflichtig bestellen' or equally clear); otherwise no contract is formed.

unordered_goods.title: Received something you didn't order: you don't have to pay
unordered_goods.summary: If a company sends you goods or services you did not order, it gets no claim against you: you do not have to pay, send them back or keep them safe. Exceptions: if it was obviously sent to you by mistake and you could see that, or if you ordered and got an equivalent substitute with a note that you may refuse it at the seller's cost.

data_access.title: You can ask any company what data it has about you
data_access.summary: Under the GDPR you can ask any company, landlord, employer or university whether and which personal data it stores about you, and get a free copy. You do not need to give a reason. They must answer within one month; in complex cases they may extend by two months but must tell you within the first month.

discrimination_housing.title: Rejected for a flat because of your origin: that is illegal
discrimination_housing.summary: Landlords and estate agents may not treat you worse when renting because of your ethnic origin (also national origin). This applies even to small private landlords. In January 2026 the BGH confirmed that estate agents are liable too. You can claim damages and compensation, but you must do so within two months, in writing. Keep evidence (e.g. same application under another name).

abmahnung_cap.title: Copyright warning letter: lawyer fees are capped for private people
abmahnung_cap.summary: If a private person who did not use the work commercially receives a first warning letter (Abmahnung), the lawyer fees they can be asked to pay are calculated on a value of max. 1,000 EUR for the injunction claim. This does not cap damages. A warning letter that does not meet the transparency rules of § 97a Abs. 2 UrhG is invalid. Do not ignore the deadline and do not sign the attached declaration before it is checked.

job_search_after_degree.title: Non-EU graduates: up to 18 months to look for a job after your degree
job_search_after_degree.summary: If you finished a degree in Germany on a study permit (§ 16b or § 16c AufenthG), you can get a residence permit to look for a job for up to 18 months. It is granted directly after the studies, it allows any kind of work while you search, and you must be able to support yourself. The 18 months cannot be extended.

blocked_account_amount.title: Student visa: proof of funds is 992 EUR a month in 2026
blocked_account_amount.summary: For a study visa or residence permit (§ 16b AufenthG) you must show at least 992 EUR a month, i.e. 11,904 EUR a year in 2026. You can prove it with a blocked account (Sperrkonto), a scholarship confirmation or a Verpflichtungserklärung. Other purposes, for example looking for a place at university, have a higher amount (1,091 EUR a month in 2026).

residence_permit_extension.title: Applied to extend your residence permit in time: the old one keeps working
residence_permit_extension.summary: If you apply to extend your residence permit, or for a different one, before it expires, the old permit counts as continuing until the Ausländerbehörde decides. This happens by law, even if the authority is slow. Work permission you had usually continues too. You can ask for a Fiktionsbescheinigung as proof. A late application generally does not have this effect automatically.

written_contract_terms.title: Your employer must give you the key terms of the job in writing
written_contract_terms.summary: Under the Nachweisgesetz the employer must record the essential terms of your job and hand them to you, even if the contract was agreed only by mouth. Since 1 January 2025 text form (for example an email) is enough, but you can still ask for it on paper. Names of the parties, pay and working hours are due on the first working day; the other terms within a month at the latest.

fixed_term_needs_writing.title: A fixed-term job only works if the end date is in a signed contract
fixed_term_needs_writing.summary: A fixed-term employment contract needs the fixed term in writing, signed by hand, and the signed document must reach you before the job starts (BAG, 7 AZR 756/14). If the term was only agreed by mouth or signed after you began, it is void and you have an open-ended job (§ 16 TzBfG). Only the fixed term needs this form, not the contract as a whole.

dismissal_three_weeks.title: Fired: you have only 3 weeks to go to the labour court
dismissal_three_weeks.summary: If you want to challenge a written dismissal, you must file a lawsuit at the labour court within three weeks after you receive it. This applies in small companies and in the first six months too, not only in firms covered by the main dismissal protection rules. If you miss the deadline, the dismissal counts as valid even if it was wrong.

holiday_pay.title: Public holiday on a work day: you get paid, even in a Minijob
holiday_pay.summary: If a public holiday falls on a day you would normally have worked, the employer must pay you what you would have earned (§ 2 EFZG). This applies to part-timers and Minijobbers too. The employer may not make you work the hours before or after on another day. If you would not have worked that day anyway, there is no extra holiday pay.

sick_notification.title: Calling in sick: tell your employer at once, a doctor confirms from day 4
sick_notification.summary: You must tell your employer immediately that you cannot work and how long it will probably last. If it lasts longer than three calendar days, a doctor must confirm it by the next working day. For people in statutory health insurance the doctor sends it electronically (eAU) and the employer retrieves it. The employer may ask for the confirmation earlier, even from the first day. You do not have to tell your employer the diagnosis.

tips_belong_to_you.title: Tips belong to you, are tax-free and do not count toward minimum wage
tips_belong_to_you.summary: Tips that customers give voluntarily are legally yours, not the employer's. They are tax-free (§ 3 Nr. 51 EStG) and can not be counted against the minimum wage. A contract may lower your pay because tips are expected, but it may not exclude pay altogether. If the employer pools tips, it must share them fairly and may not keep a part.

overtime_flat_clause.title: 'All overtime is covered by your salary' is usually invalid
overtime_flat_clause.summary: A contract clause saying that overtime is covered by the salary is invalid if it does not say how many hours (BAG, 5 AZR 517/09). Such a clause has to be clear and limited. A clause like 'the first 20 overtime hours a month are included' can be valid (BAG, 5 AZR 331/11). Without a valid clause, overtime must be paid or compensated with time off.

minijob_pension.title: Minijob: pension contribution of 3.6 percent, you can opt out
minijob_pension.summary: In a commercial Minijob the employer pays 15 percent into the pension fund and you pay 3.6 percent yourself, unless you apply to your employer for an exemption in writing or electronically. If you opt out you keep more net pay but lose pension benefits. From 1 July 2026 you can undo an exemption once, for the future (§ 6 Abs. 6 SGB VI).

discriminated_application.title: Rejected for a job because of discrimination: compensation claim, 2-month deadline
discriminated_application.summary: If you were turned down for a job because of race, ethnic origin, gender, religion, disability, age or sexual identity, you can claim compensation under § 15 AGG. You must claim it in writing within two months, starting with the rejection, and sue within three months after that (§ 61b ArbGG). If you would not have got the job anyway, the compensation is capped at three monthly salaries. The law gives no right to the job itself.

bafoeg_repayment.title: BAföG repayment: half is a grant, you repay at most 10,010 EUR
bafoeg_repayment.summary: Student BAföG is usually paid half as a grant and half as an interest-free loan. Of the loan you repay at most 10,010 EUR, however much you received. Repayment normally starts five years after the end of the maximum funding period, with instalments of at least 130 EUR a month. After 77 instalments the debt is cleared. If you earn little, you can apply for lower instalments or an exemption.

bafoeg_change_subject.title: Switching subject or dropping out: BAföG goes on only if you switch early
bafoeg_change_subject.summary: BAföG for a new subject (or after dropping out) is only continued if there is an important reason and the switch happens before the start of the 4th semester. After that you need an 'unabweisbarer Grund' (a reason you could not avoid). A plain change of interest (Neigungswandel) no longer counts after the end of the 3rd semester.

bafoeg_apply_early.title: BAföG is not paid retroactively: apply in the first month
bafoeg_apply_early.summary: BAföG is paid from the month in which your application reaches the BAföG office, at the earliest from the start of your studies, not for earlier months. So a late application loses whole months. A short informal application is enough to secure the month; you can hand in the forms and documents later.

bafoeg_side_job.title: BAföG and a side job: about 603 EUR a month is not counted in 2026
bafoeg_side_job.summary: You can work alongside BAföG. In 2026 income up to the Minijob limit of 603 EUR a month (about 7,237 EUR gross a year) does not reduce your BAföG. Above that, the excess is counted against your BAföG over the approval period. What counts is when the money reaches your account, not when you worked.

kindergeld_side_job.title: Kindergeld: no income limit in your first degree, 20-hour limit in a second
kindergeld_side_job.summary: There is no income limit for Kindergeld any more. In a first training or first degree your parents keep Kindergeld whatever you earn on the side. For a second training or second degree they get it only if you work no more than 20 hours a week (or the job is part of the training). Changing or restarting a degree before finishing one still counts as the first.

family_insurance_limit.title: Free family insurance: income limit 565 EUR a month (603 EUR in a Minijob)
family_insurance_limit.summary: You stay free of charge in your parents' statutory health insurance only while your regular monthly income stays under the limit: 565 EUR in 2026, or 603 EUR if your only job is a Minijob. Other income such as rent or self-employment counts too. If you exceed it, you must insure yourself, usually in the student scheme. A short overshoot of about two months a year can be tolerated; ask your Krankenkasse before taking a job.

werkstudent_contributions.law: Werkstudentenprivileg (§ 6 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 SGB V, § 27 Abs. 4 SGB III)
werkstudent_contributions.title: Werkstudent: only pension contributions, no health or unemployment insurance
werkstudent_contributions.summary: As a Werkstudent you and your employer pay no health, long-term care or unemployment insurance contributions on your pay, only pension insurance, which you share half and half. This only holds while you work no more than 20 hours a week in total, counting all jobs together. Above that, all insurance branches become mandatory. You still need your own student health insurance.

rent_arrears_termination.title: Late rent: when the landlord can end your lease at once, and how to stop it
rent_arrears_termination.summary: A landlord can end a flat lease without notice if you are behind with more than one month's rent for two months in a row, or the arrears reach two months' rent. If you pay all arrears within two months after the landlord has sued for eviction (Schonfrist), that termination becomes void. An ordinary notice based on the same arrears can still stay valid (BGH, VIII ZR 106/23).

warranty_twelve_months.title: Faulty product: 2 years warranty, the seller must prove it's not a defect in the first 12 months
warranty_twelve_months.summary: When you buy from a business, defects are covered for two years (§ 438 BGB). If the defect shows up within 12 months of delivery, it is presumed to have been there from the start, and the seller has to prove otherwise (§ 477 Abs. 1 BGB; before 2022 this was 6 months). The BGH ruled in May 2026 that the seller cannot escape this just because other causes are conceivable. For second-hand goods the period can be shortened by contract to one year.

flight_delay_compensation.title: Flight delayed 3 hours or more: 250 to 600 EUR compensation
flight_delay_compensation.summary: If your flight reaches its final destination 3 hours or more late, you can claim compensation under EU Regulation 261/2004: 250 EUR up to 1,500 km, 400 EUR for 1,500 to 3,500 km (and for longer flights within the EU), 600 EUR beyond that. It applies if the flight starts in the EU or the airline is based in the EU. There is no payment if the delay was caused by extraordinary circumstances. On many routes the airline must also give you meals and drinks from 2 hours of waiting.

internship_holiday.title: Internship: holiday and a reference only for voluntary internships
internship_holiday.summary: In a voluntary internship (§ 26 BBiG) you have a right to paid holiday under the Federal Holiday Act, to a written reference and to appropriate pay for work that teaches you a job. In a compulsory internship required by your study regulations there is no holiday entitlement.

termination_without_notice.title: Fired or quitting without notice: you need an important reason and act within 2 weeks
termination_without_notice.summary: A termination without notice (fristlos) is only valid with an important reason that makes it unreasonable to continue until the end of the notice period (§ 626 Abs. 1 BGB). It can only be declared within two weeks after the person learned the reason (§ 626 Abs. 2 BGB); after that it is invalid. This applies to employer and employee. Employees can also quit without notice for serious reasons such as unpaid wages.

semester_fee_deadline.law: Immatrikulationssatzung / Landeshochschulgesetz (varies by state and university)
semester_fee_deadline.title: Semester fee: paying it on time is your re-registration, late payment costs a fee
semester_fee_deadline.summary: At most universities you re-register for the next semester simply by paying the semester fee within the re-registration period, normally towards the end of the running semester. What counts is the day the money arrives, not the day you send it, so an instant transfer on the last day can still be late. After the deadline there is usually a late fee, often between 4 and 30 EUR depending on the university. If you pay nothing at all you get exmatriculated, but if you pay the fee and the late charge afterwards the exmatriculation is usually reversed. Deadlines and amounts are set by your own university.

semester_ticket_price.title: Deutschland-Semesterticket: 37.80 EUR a month (226.80 EUR a semester) from winter 2026/27
semester_ticket_price.summary: The student Deutschland-Semesterticket is priced at 60 percent of the regular Deutschlandticket. The regular ticket costs 63 EUR from January 2026, so the student price rises from 34.80 EUR to 37.80 EUR a month, which is 226.80 EUR per semester from the winter semester 2026/27. Where your university has the solidarity model, you pay it with your semester fee and a refund is only possible in defined exceptional cases.

kindergeld_six_months.title: Kindergeld is paid back for six months at most: apply early
kindergeld_six_months.summary: Kindergeld is paid retroactively only for the last six months before the month in which your application reaches the Familienkasse, even if you were entitled for longer. The Federal Fiscal Court confirmed this limit in 2024. Months older than that are lost. So send the enrolment certificate as soon as you start studying, and apply even if you are not sure yet.

kindergeld_gap_months.title: Kindergeld between school and studies: up to 4 months without a gap
kindergeld_gap_months.summary: Your parents keep getting Kindergeld for a gap of at most four months between two training stages, for example between finishing school and starting your degree. The gap can also fall between a finished stage and the next one, but Kindergeld stops if you are not in a place or have not applied for one. Kindergeld also runs to the end of the official training period even if you passed your final exam earlier. Your own income no longer matters in a first degree.

exam_final_fail.title: Failed an exam for the last time: exmatriculation is the rule, but you have options
exam_final_fail.summary: At Bavarian universities you must be exmatriculated once you have finally failed an exam that your degree requires, unless you switch to another degree (Art. 49 BayHSchG). How many retakes you get is set in your Prüfungsordnung: under the general rules for Bavarian universities of applied sciences an exam can usually be repeated once without conditions, and in many programmes a second retake follows. Some regulations allow a further attempt in a hardship case on request. You can object to the notice of final failure and later sue, and a final fail often blocks the same degree at other German universities.

student_insurance_no_semester_limit.title: Student health insurance: no 14-semester limit any more, only the age limit of 30
student_insurance_no_semester_limit.summary: The compulsory student health insurance ends with the semester in which you turn 30. Until 2020 it also ended after the 14th subject semester. That limit was dropped, so a long study period alone no longer pushes you into the voluntary, more expensive insurance. In exceptional cases, such as a long illness or having a child, it can last past 30. Doctoral students are not covered by it.

rent_brake_complaint.title: Rent too high: send a written complaint (Rüge) to get overpaid rent back
rent_brake_complaint.summary: Only after a written complaint (Rüge) to your landlord can you reclaim rent that exceeded the Mietpreisbremse. For contracts signed from 1 April 2020 you get back the overpayment from the start of the lease if you complain within 30 months of the start; if you complain later you only get money back for rent due after the complaint. For contracts from 2019 on, a simple sentence saying the rent is higher than allowed is enough. Keep paying, but state that you pay under reservation of reclaim. If several people rent the flat, one complaint works for all of them.

withdrawal_exceptions.title: Online withdrawal: when the 14 days start and which goods are excluded
withdrawal_exceptions.summary: The 14 days begin when you receive the goods, and it is enough to send your withdrawal before they run out. If the shop did not properly tell you about your right, it lasts up to 12 months and 14 days. Some contracts have no right of withdrawal at all (§ 312g Abs. 2 BGB), for example goods made to your specifications, sealed hygiene products once unsealed, or software whose seal you broke. Buying in a shop is not covered by the right at all.

broadcast_fee_wg.title: Shared flat: the broadcasting fee is one per flat, an exempt flatmate doesn't free the others
broadcast_fee_wg.summary: The Rundfunkbeitrag (18.36 EUR a month) is charged per flat, not per person. If one flatmate gets BAföG and is exempt, the others still have to pay the full fee. Only if every flatmate is exempt does the flat pay nothing. An exemption only lasts for the BAföG approval period and has to be applied for again afterwards. Students who get no BAföG can only be exempt in hardship cases, for example a second degree, a late subject change or exceeding the funding period.

wohngeld_exceptions.title: Housing benefit exceptions: BAföG only as a loan, over the age limit, second degree
wohngeld_exceptions.summary: Students who could in principle get BAföG are excluded from Wohngeld, because BAföG already contains a housing part. It is possible if your BAföG is paid only as a full loan, or if you have no BAföG entitlement in principle, for example because you are over the age limit, past the funding period, in a late subject change or in a second degree. It is not possible if the only reason for missing BAföG is that your own or your parents' income is too high. A flat shared with people who are not students or trainees can also be eligible.

intl_work_20h.title: Non-EU students: the 20-hours-a-week alternative to the 140-day rule
intl_work_20h.summary: Besides the 140 full or 280 half days a year, students from non-EU countries can alternatively work up to 20 hours a week during lecture periods, like students from the EU. In the lecture-free time more than 20 hours are allowed as long as you stay within the yearly 140-day allowance. The calculation can be tricky, so ask your Ausländerbehörde or university advice service before starting a job.

intl_compulsory_internship.title: Non-EU students: which internships and days count towards the 140 days
intl_compulsory_internship.summary: Voluntary internships count towards the 140 full or 280 half working days a year, but compulsory internships required by your study regulations do not. Days of holiday or sickness are not counted either; only days you actually work are. A half day is a workday of up to four hours. If you want to work more than the allowance you need the permission of the Ausländerbehörde before you start.

tax_allowance_2026.law: § 32a EStG; § 9a EStG; § 46 Abs. 2 Nr. 8 EStG; § 169 AO
tax_allowance_2026.title: Tax-free allowance 2026: 12,348 EUR a year, and a tax return is usually optional
tax_allowance_2026.summary: In 2026 the first 12,348 EUR of your yearly taxable income is tax-free (Grundfreibetrag), and an employee lump sum of 1,230 EUR for job costs is deducted automatically. Most working students are not obliged to file a return. It becomes compulsory if you are self-employed or have several employers at the same time. You can file voluntarily and have four years for it, which is the usual way to get withheld wage tax back.
keywords: how much can i earn tax free

second_home_tax_munich.title: Munich: students with a registered secondary residence pay Zweitwohnungsteuer
second_home_tax_munich.summary: Munich charges a Zweitwohnungsteuer on a flat you use in addition to your main residence, and it applies to you even if your main residence is only your old room at your parents' place. The rate in Munich is 18 percent of the yearly net cold rent. The city sends you a declaration form when you register a secondary residence, and the tax is due by 1 July. Courts have confirmed that students must pay it, which is why many cities want students to make their study town the main residence. Ask the Munich tax office whether an exemption applies to you.

kfw_study_loan.title: KfW study loan: 100 to 650 EUR a month, variable interest of 6.53 percent since April 2026
kfw_study_loan.summary: The KfW-Studienkredit pays students between 100 and 650 EUR a month, needs no collateral and can be combined with BAföG. The interest is variable and was raised to an effective 6.53 percent a year on 1 April 2026. It is adjusted every six months, on 1 April and 1 October, so check the current rate at KfW before you sign. Interest is already deducted from the payouts. Compared with it, the separate Bildungskredit is cheaper but only for the final phase of studies.

leave_semester_bafoeg.title: Leave of absence (Urlaubssemester): no BAföG, tell the BAföG office at once
leave_semester_bafoeg.summary: During a Urlaubssemester you have no BAföG entitlement. You have to tell the BAföG office immediately, and BAföG you already received for that time is claimed back, even if the leave is granted retroactively. Not reporting it can be an administrative offence with a fine. Whether your parents keep getting Kindergeld depends on the reason for the leave, for example it can continue if you prepare for an exam. You may be able to claim Wohngeld during the leave, because you have no BAföG entitlement then.

leave_semester_exams.title: On leave from university (beurlaubt): usually no courses and no exams
leave_semester_exams.summary: While you are beurlaubt you normally may not attend courses or sit exams, and you cannot take the credits. Exceptions exist: at many universities you may retake failed exams that do not need a course, and exams for which the reason for the leave did not yet exist at registration. People on maternity protection or parental leave can usually continue to study. A leave is not possible at some universities once you have taken part in an exam that semester. Ask your Prüfungsamt before you apply.

cheating_plagiarism.law: Prüfungsordnung; § 6 RaPO (Bavarian universities of applied sciences)
cheating_plagiarism.title: Cheating or plagiarism: failed exam, in serious cases final fail or exmatriculation
cheating_plagiarism.summary: Under most exam regulations a cheating attempt is enough to fail the exam, usually graded 5.0 or non-passed; carrying a forbidden aid can already count even if you did not use it. Plagiarism means using a source without naming it, and some universities treat it as a cheating attempt even if it happened by accident. AI tools count if your examiner has not allowed them. Serious or repeated cases can lead to the exam being finally failed or to exmatriculation. The exam office has to prove the cheating, and you can object to a decision.

nachteilsausgleich_deadline.title: Nachteilsausgleich: ask before the exam, you can't get it afterwards
nachteilsausgleich_deadline.summary: A Nachteilsausgleich such as extra writing time must be applied for before the exam, usually with a medical certificate, and at many universities by a set deadline, sometimes weeks ahead. You cannot get it retroactively after failing an exam. You can suggest a measure in your application but the exam board is not bound to it and decides on its own. If the board approves, this is not marked on your certificate. An application is not the same as registering for the exam, you need both.

probation_fixed_term.title: Fixed-term job: a probation as long as the contract doesn't give short notice
probation_fixed_term.summary: Even in a fixed-term job you can only end the contract early by ordinary notice if the contract says so. A probation period with the short two-week notice must be in proportion to the length of the contract. The Federal Labour Court held that a probation covering the whole fixed term is disproportionate, so the normal notice of four weeks to the 15th or the end of a month applies instead. The dismissal is still valid, only the notice period changes.

reference_details.title: Job reference: written on paper, qualified on request, truthful but benevolent
reference_details.summary: Every employee, including part-timers, side-job holders and Minijobbers, has a right to a written reference when the job ends. It must be on paper, an electronic form is excluded. A simple reference only states job and duration; on request it must also judge your performance and conduct (qualified reference). It has to be truthful but written benevolently so it doesn't unfairly block your career, and it must be clear without hidden messages. You can ask for an interim reference (Zwischenzeugnis) if you have a justified interest, for example when you have been given notice.

overtime_proof.title: Overtime pay: you have to show the hours and that your employer wanted or allowed them
overtime_proof.summary: Overtime is paid if it was ordered, approved, tolerated or needed to finish the work. If you sue for overtime pay you must prove how many extra hours you worked and that your employer instigated or tolerated them. The Federal Labour Court ruled in 2022 that the duty to record working time does not change this. So write down your hours yourself, have timesheets signed, and keep emails in which your boss asks for the extra work.

student_parent_bafoeg.title: Studying with a child: BAföG child-care supplement for children under 14
student_parent_bafoeg.summary: BAföG recipients with children under 14 can apply for a separate child-care supplement for each child, and it does not have to be repaid. If you only interrupt your studies for pregnancy or maternity protection for up to three months, BAföG continues. On request the maximum funding period can be extended because of pregnancy and child care. Parental benefit (Elterngeld) above the minimum amount is counted as income against your BAföG. Maternity protection also applies to students.

mobile_price_increase.title: Mobile or internet provider raises the price: you can cancel for free for three months
mobile_price_increase.summary: If a phone or internet provider changes your contract against your will, for example with a price increase or less data, you have a special right to cancel without notice period and without costs, even during the minimum term. The right is limited to three months after you were informed. The provider must tell you on a durable medium at least one and at most two months in advance what changes and when, and that you may cancel. Cancel in writing and refer to the provider's price notice; you can keep your phone number.

schufa_free_copy.title: Schufa report: a free copy once a year, the answer must come within a month
schufa_free_copy.summary: Under Art. 15 GDPR you can get a free copy of the data the Schufa holds about you at least once a year, without giving a reason, and it must answer within one month. A copy after you have had errors corrected is free again. The online instant information is a paid product, around 30 EUR, so use the free postal or portal copy instead. Check it for wrong data and old entries and ask for correction or deletion in writing if something is wrong.

bafoeg_flexi_semester.title: BAföG after the standard period: one free extra semester (Flexi-Semester) plus extensions for specific reasons
bafoeg_flexi_semester.summary: Once in your Bachelor or Master you can get BAföG for one more semester after the standard period without giving a reason (the Flexibilitätssemester). Beyond that, BAföG can be extended for a fitting time if you went over because of serious reasons, for example a first failed final exam, a disability, pregnancy or caring for a child under 14, or caring for a relative with care level 3. You have to prove the reason and show it caused the delay, so apply early, ideally at the start of the last funded semester.

bafoeg_performance_proof.title: BAföG from the 5th semester: you need a performance record (Leistungsnachweis), usually about 120 ECTS
bafoeg_performance_proof.summary: To keep getting BAföG from the 5th subject semester you must hand in a performance record (Leistungsnachweis) showing the work normally expected by then, which in most Bachelor programmes is about 120 ECTS. It counts as handed in on time if the BAföG office receives it within four months after the semester it covers. If you are short, ask for an exception: in some cases the deadline can be extended if the funding period will probably be extended anyway. Your Prüfungsamt issues the form, so ask it early.

bafoeg_abroad.title: BAföG abroad: a full degree in the EU is funded, outside the EU one year, at least six months abroad
bafoeg_abroad.summary: You can get BAföG for studying abroad if you live permanently in Germany and the foreign university is equivalent. In the EU or Switzerland even a whole degree can be funded. Outside the EU, BAföG usually covers one year (two semesters) in one continuous stay, after at least a year of studying in Germany, in rare cases up to five semesters. The stay must last at least six months or one semester, and it must help your studies at home. Apply about six months before leaving, and mandatory internships abroad can be funded too. Up to two semesters abroad do not count towards your funding period in Germany.

liability_insurance_student.title: Liability insurance: covered by your parents' policy during a first education, but check it
liability_insurance_student.summary: Private liability insurance (Privathaftpflicht) is not compulsory, but damage you cause can be very expensive. Many parents' family policies also cover adult children during their first education or degree. It ends at the latest after the education or marriage, and several insurers end it at a second degree or around 25 years old, so check your parents' contract in writing. If you are not covered, a policy for students often costs only a few euros a month. The Verbraucherzentrale recommends a sum insured of about 10 million EUR.

health_insurance_exemption.title: Privately insured students: exemption from statutory insurance must be requested within three months and is binding
health_insurance_exemption.summary: If you are privately insured, you can choose at enrolment: switch to the statutory student insurance or ask a statutory health fund to be exempted so you can stay private. The exemption request has to be filed within three months after your studies start, and it is binding for the rest of your studies, you cannot go back to the statutory scheme later. Think about it carefully: the choice is only possible again when your status changes, for example when you take a job with social insurance.

eigenbedarf_hardship_objection.title: Notice for the landlord's own use: you can object because of hardship, at the latest two months before the end
eigenbedarf_hardship_objection.summary: A termination because of the landlord's own need must be written, signed and give a real reason. Even a valid termination can be objected to if moving out would be a hardship for you or your household, for example illness, pregnancy or not finding another flat. The objection has to reach the landlord at the latest two months before the notice period ends. The notice period is at least three months and gets longer with the years you have lived there. You cannot object to an immediate termination. Mieterverein or a lawyer can help check the notice.

rent_step_index.title: Step rent and index rent: allowed, but the rent brake still applies and a step rent is fixed in euros
rent_step_index.summary: A step rent (Staffelmiete) fixes future rent increases in the lease as amounts in euros, not percentages. It is allowed, but neither the starting rent nor later stages may exceed what the rent brake permits in a tight market. The usual 15 or 20 percent cap for rent increases does not apply to a step rent. An index rent (Indexmiete) ties your rent to the consumer price index, so it can rise with inflation. Check which model your lease has before you sign and what happens at the next stage.

energy_price_exit.title: Electricity or gas price change: you can cancel without notice period until it takes effect
energy_price_exit.summary: When your energy provider changes the price during the contract, even if it lowers it, you can cancel your electricity or gas contract without a notice period until the change takes effect. The provider has to announce the change in a clear letter that points out your special termination right. If the letter is missing this reference or is not clear, the increase is not valid. You can also object to a bill later and ask for the money back. Keep your cancellation proof and have the new provider handle the switch.

copyright_images_papers.title: Photos and texts from the internet are protected: quote with credit, and ask before publishing online
copyright_images_papers.summary: Almost every picture on the internet is protected by copyright. Using one in a paper that only your lecturer sees falls under different exceptions than publishing it online. A court case about a school presentation showed that posting a photo on a public site without permission can lead to a warning letter, even for a student. A quotation is only allowed if it is needed to support your own point, keeps its original wording and names the source. If you receive a warning letter, do not sign the demand for an undertaking before getting advice, since it can be changed.

gym_contract.title: Gym contracts: two years at most, a monthly notice after the minimum term, and no withdrawal if you signed in the studio
gym_contract.summary: Fitness studio contracts usually run for 12 or 24 months, the maximum minimum term in standard terms is two years. For contracts signed after 1 March 2022, an automatic extension is only possible for an unlimited term that you can cancel with one month's notice. If you sign in the studio itself there is normally no withdrawal right, but there is one for contracts concluded online or by phone. An early termination without notice is only possible for important reasons, a move to another town is usually not enough unless your contract says so.

semesterticket_refund.title: Semesterticket: it is a solidarity ticket, a refund is only possible in listed exceptional cases
semesterticket_refund.summary: The semester ticket is based on the Deutschlandticket and costs 60 percent of its price, which is why every student has to buy it. A refund or exemption is only possible in the exceptions in your university's ticket contract, for example a hardship case, buying the ticket twice because you are enrolled at two universities, leave of absence or a disability. Often the evidence has to be handed in before the semester fee is paid or by a deadline. The semester fee is more than the ticket, and only the ticket share is refunded.

deutschlandticket_cancel.title: Deutschlandticket subscription: cancel by the 10th of a month for the end of that month
deutschlandticket_cancel.summary: The normal Deutschlandticket subscription runs for an unlimited time and can be cancelled monthly. Your cancellation must reach the company by the 10th of the month, and then the ticket is valid until the end of that calendar month. It differs from the Deutschlandsemesterticket, which has a fixed term for the semester and cannot be cancelled monthly. Check which one you have before you cancel, since a student can have the semester ticket as the cheaper way to ride.

thesis_in_company.title: Writing your thesis at a company: only the thesis work itself does not trigger minimum wage
thesis_in_company.summary: If you write your Bachelor or Master thesis in a company and only do the work needed for the thesis, for example using the company's data and expertise, it is not a job and the minimum wage does not apply. If you also do normal work for the company, a thesis does not stop that work from being paid at least the minimum wage. Agree in writing what you do, who supervises you and whether you get paid, so that it is clear which part is thesis and which is work.

thesis_deadline_extension.title: Thesis deadline: ask for an extension in time, otherwise a missed deadline counts as 5.0
thesis_deadline_extension.summary: If you miss the hand-in date of a thesis and have not asked for an extension, the work is usually graded 5.0 or non-passed. An extension needs an important reason that you are not responsible for, for example illness, and it must be requested in time in writing. A plain sick note for being unfit for work may not be enough, since the exam office decides itself whether the problem justifies more time. Extensions are often capped, at some universities at half the normal time, and an extension of the thesis does not move other deadlines. Check your study and exam regulations.

attendance_obligation.title: Compulsory attendance: lectures normally no, labs and seminars only if your regulations say so
attendance_obligation.summary: A general attendance duty at universities is not planned and would not be allowed in that form, according to a Bavarian university answering the state parliament. In lectures there is usually no attendance duty. Attendance requirements are an exception for individual courses such as seminars, practicals or labs, and they should be set down in the course or exam regulations. Look up your Studien- und Prüfungsordnung and the module handbook, and if you were failed for missing a lecture, ask the Prüfungsamt or the student advisory service.

master_provisional_admission.title: Master application before the Bachelor is finished: allowed, but the certificate has to follow by a deadline
master_provisional_admission.summary: At many universities you can apply for a Master's programme before your Bachelor is finished. You usually hand in a transcript showing the credits so far, and the final Bachelor certificate has to follow by a set date, for example at the latest when you re-register for the second Master semester. If the certificate does not arrive on time, the provisional admission lapses. The university normally does not check if you can finish in time, that is your responsibility, so plan your thesis and the correction time. Read the rules of the programme you are applying to.

wg_joint_liability.title: Shared flat with everyone on the lease: all are liable for the whole rent and only everyone together can cancel
wg_joint_liability.summary: If all flatmates signed the lease as main tenants, they are jointly liable (Gesamtschuldner): the landlord can demand the full rent or damages from any one of them, if another does not pay. The lease can only be cancelled by all of them together, a partial cancellation by one person does not exist. Someone who just moves out stays a party to the contract and remains liable. Agree with your flatmates and the landlord how a change of flatmates works, ideally before you sign.

pets_in_flat.law: § 535 BGB; BGH VIII ZR 340/06, VIII ZR 329/11
pets_in_flat.title: Pets in a rented flat: small animals always, dogs and cats usually only with the landlord's consent
pets_in_flat.summary: Small animals like hamsters, fish or budgies belong to normal use of a flat and you do not need to ask, even if a blanket ban is in the lease. A clause that forbids all animals is invalid, according to the Federal Court of Justice. For dogs and cats the landlord can require consent, but he must look at each case, weighing the interests of both sides, and cannot refuse just by habit. Without permission he can warn you, so ask first and get the answer in writing.

phishing_bank_refund.title: Money taken from your account by fraud: your bank has to refund unauthorised payments, report it at once
phishing_bank_refund.summary: If money leaves your account without your authorisation, for example after a phishing attack, the bank must refund it under § 675u BGB, usually by the end of the next business day. Report the case to the bank immediately and in writing, say clearly that it is an unauthorised payment and ask for a refund under § 675u BGB, and report it to the police. Banks often refuse by pointing to gross negligence, and then they may claim damages from you, so keep all messages and ask a Verbraucherzentrale for help if the bank refuses. With simple negligence your liability is capped at 50 EUR.

quit_unemployment_block.title: Quitting or signing a termination agreement can block unemployment benefit for up to 12 weeks
quit_unemployment_block.summary: If you end a job yourself or sign an Aufhebungsvertrag without an important reason, the employment agency can impose a block period (Sperrzeit) of usually 12 weeks on unemployment benefit (ALG I), because it sees the unemployment as self-caused. The block does not apply if you have an important reason that you can prove. Do not sign a termination agreement on the spot, and if you sign one, keep the normal notice period, since ending the job earlier can also pause your benefit. If you only work a side job, check with the Arbeitsagentur whether you would be entitled to ALG I at all.

vacation_expiry.title: Unused holiday: it normally lapses at year end, but only if your employer warned you in time
vacation_expiry.summary: Holiday not taken in the calendar year normally lapses on 31 December. It can be carried over to 31 March of the next year only for urgent operational or personal reasons. According to the Federal Labour Court and the ECJ, statutory holiday only lapses if the employer has clearly and in time told you how many days you have left, asked you to take them and warned that they expire. Without that warning your days stay. A special rule applies after long illness. Ask for your remaining days in writing.

sunday_holiday_pay.title: Sunday, holiday and night work: time off is the law, a surcharge only for night work or by contract
sunday_holiday_pay.summary: There is no general legal right to extra pay for work on Sundays and public holidays. The law gives you a replacement day off: for a holiday within eight weeks. Only night work requires a compensation, extra pay or time off. A surcharge for Sundays and holidays can come from your contract, a collective agreement, a works agreement or a regular practice. If it is paid, it is tax-free up to 50 percent of the base wage on Sundays, 125 percent on holidays and 150 percent on 24 to 26 December and 1 May. Check your contract and payslip.

rail_delay_compensation.title: Train delay of 60 minutes: 25 percent of the fare back, 50 percent from 120 minutes
rail_delay_compensation.summary: If you arrive at your destination at least 60 minutes late, you get 25 percent of the fare for the single trip back, and from 120 minutes late 50 percent. The right is also there during strikes. Season tickets are compensated with flat amounts per delay, for local transport with a Deutschlandticket for example 1.50 EUR per case. Amounts below 4 EUR are not paid out. Apply with the railway company's form or online, and keep your delay proof and ticket, as there may be a deadline for your claim.

private_sale_warranty.title: Buying second-hand from a private seller: warranty can be excluded, but not for concealed defects
private_sale_warranty.summary: When you buy used from a private person, for example on Kleinanzeigen, the seller can exclude the statutory warranty with a clear sentence like no warranty or sold as seen. A copied half-sentence may not be enough. Such an exclusion does not protect a seller who knew about a defect and hid it or lied about the item, and you would have to prove that. So test the item, ask questions in writing and keep the ad text and messages. Dealers cannot exclude the warranty in the same way.

internet_move_cancel.title: Moving with an internet contract: it moves with you, you can only cancel if the provider can't deliver there
internet_move_cancel.summary: When you move, your internet provider has to continue the contract at the new address on unchanged terms, so a move does not shorten or extend the contract term. If the provider cannot deliver the service at your new address, you have a special right to cancel with one month's notice. According to the Verbraucherzentrale Niedersachsen this also applies if you move into a shared flat where the line is already used by another provider. Cancel in writing, name the move date and ask for confirmation.

small_business_dismissal.title: Dismissal protection: only after 6 months and in firms with more than 10 employees
small_business_dismissal.summary: The general protection against dismissal under the KSchG applies when the firm regularly employs more than 10 people (trainees not counted, part-timers counted pro rata) and your job has lasted longer than six months without a break. In a small firm or in your first six months the employer does not need one of the three KSchG reasons. Even then a dismissal still has to follow the general rules, for example written form, notice periods, and it must not be discriminatory or abusive. If you are unsure whether the KSchG applies to you, free advice from a union or an Arbeitsrechtsberatung is worth it, because the deadline to sue is short.

maternity_protection_students.title: Pregnant students: maternity protection applies at university, without an application
maternity_protection_students.summary: Since 1 January 2018 the Mutterschutzgesetz also covers students, as far as place, time and course of a class are mandatory or when a compulsory internship is part of the degree. Maternity protection has to be granted in principle without a separate application. Protection periods run six weeks before the expected birth and at least eight weeks after it. You can waive some protections yourself in writing and take them back at any time. Tell your university early, because it must then assess risks and set protection measures, and you are entitled to compensation for disadvantages such as missed exams. Your Studienbüro or the equal-opportunities office can explain the details.

student_accident_insurance.title: Accident at university: students are covered by statutory accident insurance
student_accident_insurance.summary: Enrolled students are covered by the statutory accident insurance for study-related activities that have a direct connection in time and place to the university. It also covers the direct way to and from the university, and private detours such as lunch in the canteen are treated separately. Courts have refused cover to people who only sat in on a lecture without being enrolled or registered as guest students. Leisure accidents are not covered, and neither are most jobs on the side. If you are hurt at university, report it to the university and see a doctor who handles accident insurance.

side_job_approval.title: Second job: your employer cannot ban it generally, but you may have to report it
side_job_approval.summary: As an employee you may take a side job next to your main job. Your contract or a collective agreement can require you to report it and in some cases to get permission, and then you must follow that. A blanket ban on any side job in the contract is not valid. Your employer can object in individual cases, for example if the second job competes with the firm, harms your main job or breaks the working-time limits. Check your contract for a Nebentätigkeitsklausel before you start.
keywords: can my employer forbid second job

trial_work_unpaid.title: Probearbeiten: unpaid only if you are just getting to know the firm
trial_work_unpaid.summary: A short trial day can be unpaid if it is only a get-to-know-each-other visit (Einfühlungsverhältnis): you mostly watch, ask questions and try something briefly, without a duty to work and without instructions. The minimum wage does not apply then. If you actually work like an employee, you can have a claim to normal pay even if the employer called it a trial. There is no law on the length: up to a week is described as allowed, but usually it is only a day or two, and the longer it lasts the more likely it counts as an employment. Ask before you go how long it lasts and whether it is paid.
keywords: do i get paid for trial day

exam_grade_improvement.title: Repeating a passed exam to improve the grade: depends on your regulations
exam_grade_improvement.summary: Whether you can retake an exam you already passed to improve your grade, or have a failed attempt not counted (Freiversuch), differs from university to university and sometimes from degree to degree. Many regulations allow it only once, only within a time limit, or only for a limited number of modules, and usually you have to apply. If you retake it, normally the better result counts. Read the Prüfungsordnung of your own degree or ask the Prüfungsamt before registering.

credit_recognition.title: Credit recognition: the university must prove a substantial difference to refuse
credit_recognition.summary: When you switch universities, degree programme or come back from abroad, you can apply to have earlier courses recognised. Under the Lisbon Recognition Convention the university may refuse recognition only for a substantial difference in the skills gained, and it carries the burden of proof for this. You still have to take part in the process, for example by handing in transcripts and module descriptions, and recognition needs an application. If recognition is refused, you should get reasons and can object. Ask your Prüfungsamt for the form and deadline.

deposit_separate_account.title: Rent deposit: the landlord must keep it apart from his own money
deposit_separate_account.summary: A cash deposit has to be invested by the landlord separately from his own assets at a bank, at the usual savings rate with three months notice. The interest belongs to you and increases the deposit, so you normally get it when the deposit is paid back and not each year. The landlord may only use the deposit for claims from the tenancy. The Federal Court of Justice has held that you may make the payment depend on the landlord first naming an insolvency-proof account. If the deposit was kept together with his own money, you can lose it in his insolvency, so ask for proof of the account.

quiet_hours.title: Noise and quiet hours: no nationwide rule, house rules and local rules count
quiet_hours.summary: Germany has no single nationwide set of quiet hours. They come from local rules and from your Hausordnung, which may be stricter. Common are night quiet from 22:00 to 6:00 and quiet all day on Sundays and public holidays, and some house rules add a lunch break. During night hours you should keep to room volume. Parties in a flat are generally allowed within a normal volume, but there is no general exception to the quiet hours. Repeated breaches can lead to a warning from the landlord, so talk to neighbours first and check your Hausordnung.

bike_theft_insurance.title: Bike stolen: home contents insurance often pays only for theft from home, cellar or garage
bike_theft_insurance.summary: A bike is often covered by home contents insurance only when it is stolen in a break-in from the flat, cellar or garage. If it is taken from the street, which is simple theft, you only get a payout if you added extra cover for it. Policies commonly require that the bike was locked with a proper lock. Alternatively a separate bike insurance exists. Keep the receipt, the frame number and photos of the bike and lock, report the theft to the police and read your policy conditions.

fare_dodging_fee.title: No valid ticket: 60 euro fee, reduced if you show a personal ticket afterwards
fare_dodging_fee.summary: Travelling without a valid ticket usually costs a raised fare of 60 euros under the transport conditions. If you forgot a personal subscription or Deutschlandticket that was issued in your name, you can show it afterwards to the transport company that demands the fee, and then only a small processing fee is normally due. For a transferable ticket the full 60 euros is demanded. If the ticket machine was broken, the company usually waives it when this can be shown. Do not ignore the letter: if you pay nothing, the company can sue, and repeat cases can lead to a criminal complaint.

bank_account_termination.title: Bank closing your account: ordinary notice is generally at least two months
bank_account_termination.summary: A bank can end your current account with ordinary notice, which in general must be at least two months, and it does not have to give a reason or consider your interests for it. For an immediate termination there must be an important reason that makes it unreasonable to keep the account, for example misuse for illegal activity. Your overdraft limit can also be cut by the bank, so watch the messages it sends. If you think the termination is wrong, you can turn to the bank's ombudsman. Open another account early so your salary and rent payments do not stop.

handover_protocol.title: Flat handover: write down every defect in a protocol, on move-in and move-out
handover_protocol.summary: There is no required form for a handover, but you should record all defects in a signed protocol when you move in and again when you move out. Damage that is not in the protocol is difficult for the landlord to claim later, and your move-in protocol shows what was already there before you came. If you cannot attend the move-out handover you may send a person you trust. Add meter readings, take photos in daylight and do not sign anything you disagree with without adding your own note.
keywords: landlord claims damage after move out

smoke_detectors_bavaria.title: Smoke detectors in Bavaria: landlord installs, tenant usually checks them
smoke_detectors_bavaria.summary: Smoke detectors are compulsory in Bavaria: for new buildings since 2013 and for existing flats since 1 January 2018. The owner or landlord has to install them, and in Bavaria the upkeep (checking that they work) normally lies with the tenant, unless the owner takes it over. Replacing a broken detector is part of keeping the flat in repair and so is the landlord's cost. If you find none in your flat, ask the landlord in writing. Check your lease for any clause on this.

heating_cost_cut.title: Heating bill not based on your consumption: you may cut your share by 15 percent
heating_cost_cut.summary: If heating and hot water are not billed by consumption although the Heizkostenverordnung requires it, you may reduce your share of these costs by 15 percent. The right cannot be excluded in the lease. The cut applies to your share shown in the bill, not to your monthly advance payments. It only takes effect once you tell the landlord that you use it. If the bill is correct but only partly wrong, a smaller cut of 3 percent may apply for missing information. Check the bill and keep a copy of your letter.

second_degree_bafoeg.title: Second degree: usually no BAföG, but a Master after a Bachelor is not one
second_degree_bafoeg.summary: BAföG normally supports a first degree. For a second degree you generally do not get it, with exceptions such as a change of focus, a justified change of subject or a dropped first degree. A Master after a finished Bachelor does not count as a second degree under BAföG, so you can apply for BAföG for the Master. In a second degree there may also be fees and different rules for repayment, so ask your Amt für Ausbildungsförderung before you start.

forced_exmatriculation.title: Exmatriculation: what ends your enrolment and what you can still do
forced_exmatriculation.summary: In Bavaria you are exmatriculated automatically when you finish your degree, when you have finally failed a required exam, or when you do not re-register in time. You can also apply for it yourself, for example if you drop out. An exception can apply if you switch to another degree before the final fail.
